Aerobic System

This system operates through three stages: glycolysis, Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain, producing up to 38 ATP molecules per glucose molecule. While slow to reach peak output requiring 2 to 3 minutes, it can sustain ATP production indefinitely given adequate oxygen and fuel availability from carbohydrates and fats. the one idea

why this one carries the topic.

Your body has three ways to make ATP and which one runs depends entirely on how hard and how long. Everything about training follows from that.

The aerobic system uses oxygen to fully break down glucose through three stages, yielding high ATP output but requiring several minutes to reach maximum capacity.

what examiners catch — Examiners test whether students can identify the correct ATP yield (32-38 ATP) and explain why onset time (2-3 minutes) makes it unsuitable for sprint events.
what you leave with

three things, not forty.

  • Becomes predominant after 2 minutes and sustains low to moderate intensity exercise indefinitely
  • Produces 38 ATP per glucose molecule compared to 2 ATP from glycolysis alone
  • Utilizes carbohydrates and fats as fuel with protein contributing minimally during prolonged exercise
